extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. Unlike existing benchmarks, MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MMMU dataset was meticulously curated through a three-stage process. First, common university majors were reviewed to select subjects based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in those subjects. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Third, to control data quality, two steps of data cleaning were performed: identifying potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by a review by authors to eliminate duplications, and distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data sources included college exams, quizzes, and textbooks spanning six common disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. The questions were collected from major textbooks and online resources, with a focus on avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process was conducted over several months, with the final dataset compiled by June 2024.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing involved two main steps: 1) Identifying and removing potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by a review by authors to eliminate duplications. 2) Distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation protocol involved recruiting over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The questions were categorized into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard, with approximately 10% of the problems classified as very easy and excluded from the benchmark due to their simplistic nature.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotation process utilized a user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification, which significantly improved the workflow for data curation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation analysis involved a rigorous process of maintaining the quality and difficulty of the problem set. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark. This rigorous process played a crucial role in maintaining the quality and difficulty of the problem set.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The number of human labels per dataset item varied, with some questions having multiple images and annotations. The dataset includes 11.5K questions, with an average question length of 59.33, average option length of 9.17, and average explanation length of 107.92.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators were over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various disciplines and subjects. They were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The dataset utilized a user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification, which significantly improved the workflow for data curation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is maintained and updated by the core contributors, with a focus on ensuring the quality and difficulty of the problem set. The dataset is released under the MIT License, and updates are planned to include additional questions and subfields to cover a broader range of disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models (LMMs) can achieve by assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains. It provides a comprehensive benchmark that aligns with the expectations of skilled adults in these fields, potentially stimulating the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases due to the manual curation process and the focus on college-level subjects. The selection of subjects and subfields was based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in those subjects, which may introduce biases towards certain disciplines and image types.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. However, the authors argue that strong performance on this benchmark should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system. The challenging nature of MMMU is evident from the performance of over 30 models and human experts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, testing, and validation of large multimodal models (LMMs) and text-only LLMs. It can be used to evaluate the capabilities of LMMs in the context of Expert AGI by assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains. The dataset is also useful for fine-tuning models to improve their performance on expert-level tasks.
